A total of 957,342 single cells across 22 colorectal cancer (CRC) patients and 166 matched biopsy samples were analyzed across peripheral blood (417,162 cells; 43.58%), adjacent normal mucosa (260,294 cells; 27.19%), and tumor tissue (279,886 cells; 29.24%).

- Peripheral Blood (417,162 cells): Dominated by circulating immune cells, including T cells (67.08%, 279,831 cells), Myeloid cells (12.35%, 51,499 cells), B cells (10.34%, 43,131 cells), and ILC/NK cells (9.74%, 40,646 cells). Non-hematopoietic cells are virtually absent (Epithelial: 0.35%, 1,459 cells; Stromal: 0.14%, 596 cells).
  Specific circulating subsets highly restricted to blood (>97% in blood; Ro/e > 2.20) include naive CD4 T cells (c01_CD4_Tn_CCR7, c02_CD4_Tn_SELL), naive CD8 T cells (c15_CD8_Tn_CCR7), effector memory CD8 T cells (c24_CD8_Temra_CX3CR1), classical/non-classical monocytes (c50_Mono_FCGR3A, c51_Mono_NFKBIZ), NK cells (c35_ILC_FCGR3A, c33_ILC_GZMK), naive B cells (c39_NaiveB_TCL1A), and double-positive T cells (c32_DPT).

- Adjacent Normal Tissue (260,294 cells): Reflects non-malignant mucosal tissue architecture, consisting of Epithelial cells (35.62%, 92,721 cells), T cells (27.89%, 72,596 cells), B/Plasma cells (24.85%, 64,693 cells), Stromal cells (8.89%, 23,131 cells), Myeloid cells (1.82%, 4,737 cells), and ILCs (0.93%, 2,416 cells).
  Normal-enriched subsets (>65% in normal mucosa; Ro/e > 2.45) include differentiated absorptive colonocytes (c86_Coloncyte_BEST4, c84_Coloncyte_CA2), secretory Goblet and Tuft cells (c87_Goblet_MUC2, c89_Tuft_PTGS1, c88_EEC_PCSK1N), mucosal IgA plasma cells (c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1, 70.67% in normal), and tissue-homeostatic stromal subsets (c73_Fibro_ADAMDEC1, c76_Fibro_PI16, c75_Fibro_CCL19, c74_Fibro_C7, c83_Glia_PLP1).

- Tumor Tissue (279,886 cells): Marked by profound immune infiltration into neoplastic tissue: T cells (42.50%, 118,957 cells), Epithelial cells (28.22%, 78,975 cells), B/Plasma cells (17.03%, 47,678 cells), Stromal cells (6.23%, 17,434 cells), Myeloid cells (4.15%, 11,606 cells), and ILCs (1.87%, 5,236 cells). Infiltration of myeloid cells is elevated 2.28-fold (4.15% vs 1.82%) and T cells 1.52-fold (42.50% vs 27.89%) relative to adjacent normal tissue.

2. CELL TYPES SPECIFICALLY AND HIGHLY ENRICHED ONLY IN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT

Using objective statistical criteria—ratio of observed to expected frequency (Ro/e > 3.10), high tumor restriction (>90% of all cells in the cohort found in tumor), depletion in normal tissue (Ro/e <= 0.25) and blood (Ro/e <= 0.07), and donor-paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.005)—exactly 8 sub-cell-types are specifically and highly enriched only within the tumor microenvironment:

   - Total: 2,842 cells | Tumor: 2,807 (98.77%) | Normal: 35 (1.23%) | Blood: 0 (0.00%)
   - Ro/e: Tumor = 3.38, Normal = 0.05, Blood = 0.00 | Paired FDR = 9.94e-05
   - Biological role: FAP+ CAFs mediating dense desmoplasia, extracellular matrix stiffening, and exclusion of cytotoxic lymphocytes.

   - Ro/e: Tumor = 3.37, Normal = 0.05, Blood = 0.01 | Paired FDR = 3.10e-05

   - Total: 2,513 cells | Tumor: 2,442 (97.17%) | Normal: 68 (2.71%) | Blood: 3 (0.12%)
   - Ro/e: Tumor = 3.32, Normal = 0.10, Blood = 0.00 | Paired FDR = 3.04e-05

   - Ro/e: Tumor = 3.30, Normal = 0.12, Blood = 0.00 | Paired FDR = 5.25e-04
   - Biological role: Actively cycling endothelial cells reflecting ongoing neo-angiogenesis within the tumor bed.

5. c09_CD4_Th1_CXCL13_HAVCR2 (Exhausted/Dysfunctional CXCL13+ CD4 T Cells):

In colorectal cancer (CRC) patients receiving anti-PD-1 immunotherapy (GSE236581 cohort, N = 22 patients), the correlation between tumor regression ratio and baseline (pre-treatment, Stage I) cell subtype proportions depends strongly on the functional identity of the cell subtype:

1. Positive Correlations:
Key immune effector and tumor-reactive lymphocyte subtypes in the pre-treatment tumor microenvironment exhibit statistically significant POSITIVE correlations with the tumor regression ratio:
- Activated regulatory T cells (`c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9`): Pearson r = +0.5045 (p = 0.0167), Spearman rho = +0.4704 (p = 0.0272).
- Exhausted CD8+ T cells (`c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN`): Pearson r = +0.4735 (p = 0.0260), Spearman rho = +0.5065 (p = 0.0162).
- Effector memory CD4+ T cells (`c10_CD4_Temra_GZMB`): Pearson r = +0.4082 (p = 0.0593), Spearman rho = +0.4828 (p = 0.0229).
- Endothelial cells (`c68_Endo_FABP5`): Pearson r = +0.4495 (p = 0.0358), Spearman rho = +0.5017 (p = 0.0174).
- Germinal center B cells (`c44_GCB_MKI67` / `c43_GCB_LRMP`): Pearson r = +0.3670 (p = 0.0929) in tumor, and r > +0.50 (p < 0.02) across all tissues.

2. Negative Correlations:
Conversely, non-immune epithelial differentiation and immunosuppressive/stromal subtypes exhibit NEGATIVE correlations with the tumor regression ratio:
- Differentiated goblet epithelial cells (`c87_Goblet_MUC2`): Pearson r = -0.3867 (p = 0.0754), Spearman rho = -0.4636 (p = 0.0298).
- Classical monocytes (`c49_Mono_CD14`): Pearson r = -0.3773 (p = 0.0835).
- Cancer-associated fibroblasts (`c79_Fibro_FAP`): Pearson r = -0.3729 (p = 0.0874).

3. Biological and Clinical Implications:
- Pre-existing tumor-infiltrating exhausted CD8+ T cells (CD8_Tex_LAYN) and activated Tregs (CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9) are hallmarks of an immunologically "hot", inflamed tumor microenvironment. In CRC, these cells are enriched in tumors with high neoantigen loads (e.g., dMMR/MSI-H).
- The positive correlation of exhausted CD8+ T cells implies that these cells are neoantigen-primed, tumor-specific effectors that are functionally suppressed by PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint signaling; upon anti-PD-1 blockade, this inhibitory signal is relieved, triggering cytotoxic re-invigoration, tumor cell killing, and dramatic clinical tumor regression.
- In contrast, tumors enriched for differentiated structural epithelial cells (e.g., MUC2+ goblet cells) or FAP+ cancer-associated fibroblasts represent immunologically "cold" or stroma-excluded phenotypes that lack baseline antitumor immune infiltration and show poor therapeutic response to PD-1 blockade alone.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. PS-Self and PS-Part proteins represent distinct molecular classes, not merely a continuum of condensation propensity. PS-Self proteins rely on low-complexity, Gly/Pro/Ser/Gln-rich prion-like disordered domains with low charge density to drive autonomous liquid-liquid phase separation through multivalent sticker-spacer interactions. PS-Part proteins are recruited clients or co-scaffolds that feature higher charge density (K/R/E/D) and aliphatic hydrophobicity (L/I/V), utilizing electrostatic and structured binding motifs to partition into condensates.
2. Classical predictors (PScore, PLAAC, catGRANULE) are effective at detecting PS-Self proteins (AUC 0.81 - 0.83), but perform poorly on PS-Part proteins (AUC 0.64 - 0.73), missing >80% of partner-dependent condensers at canonical high-specificity operating cutoffs.
3. Multi-feature classifiers (SaPS/PdPS 10-feature models) successfully learn the distinct sequence signatures of each phase-separation class (AUC ~0.99), demonstrating that partner-dependent recruitment is predictable when decoupled from self-assembly assumptions.

Identification of Top Signaling Pathways Mediating the Suppressive and Cytotoxic Function of KIR+CD8+ T Cells Against Pathogenic CD4+ T Cells in Celiac Disease (DA-11-1)

1. Executive Summary & Core Finding:
In patients with active celiac disease (CeD), KIR+CD8+ T cells act as a distinct regulatory CD8+ T cell subset endowed with potent suppressive and cytotoxic capacity against pathogenic, inflammatory CD4+ T cells. Beyond canonical MHC class I interactions (which license and guide the recognition of HLA class I complexes on target cells), our cell-cell communication and transcriptomic network analysis reveals that the suppressive function and cytotoxic targeting of pathogenic CD4+ T cells by KIR+CD8+ T cells are mediated primarily by:
   (a) Direct death-receptor apoptosis via the FASLG–FAS signaling pathway.
   (b) Granule exocytosis cytolytic machinery driven by Perforin (PRF1), Granzymes (GZMB, GZMH, GZMA), and Granulysin (GNLY).
   (c) Contact-dependent and secreted immune suppression mediated by TGF-beta (TGFB1–TGFBR1/TGFBR2).
   (d) Inhibitory checkpoint / immune modulation through C-type lectin signaling (CLEC2D/CLEC2B–KLRB1/CD161).
   (e) Synaptic adhesion and homing stabilization mediated by CD99–CD99, SELPLG–SELL (PSGL-1–L-selectin), MIF–(CD74+CD44/CXCR4), and CD2–CD58.

2. Detailed Overview of the Top Identified Signaling Pathways:

   1. FASLG / Death Receptor Pathway (FASLG - FAS):
      - Mechanism: Direct induction of extrinsic apoptosis in target cells.
      - Quantitative Evidence: Pathogenic effector CD4+ T cells in the inflamed mucosa dramatically upregulate the death receptor FAS (CD95) to 14.83% positive cells (mean expression 0.383), representing a 7.5-fold enrichment over naive CD4+ T cells (1.99% positive, mean expression 0.096). Concurrently, KIR+CD8+ T cells specifically express FASLG (9.02% positivity, mean expression 0.288) compared to 0.60% in pathogenic CD4+ T cells and 0.02% in naive CD4+ T cells. Sensitivity-adjusted CellChat modeling confirms significant communication probability (prob = 2.74e-04, p < 0.001). This explains why pathogenic CD4+ T cells are selectively susceptible to KIR+CD8+ T-cell killing in vitro.

   2. Granzyme / Perforin Cytolytic Granule Machinery (PRF1, GZMB, GZMH, GNLY, NKG7):
      - Mechanism: Perforin-dependent pore formation on target plasma membranes coupled with the directional delivery of apoptotic granzymes and antimicrobial/cytolytic granulysin.
      - Quantitative Evidence: KIR+CD8+ T cells display near-complete saturation of cytolytic transcripts: PRF1 (96.84% positive, mean expression 14.16), GZMB (97.94% positive, mean expression 16.44), GZMH (99.84% positive, mean expression 22.70), GNLY (99.53% positive, mean expression 88.74), and NKG7 (100.0% positive, mean expression 80.08). In contrast, conventional CD4+ T cells show near-zero expression of GZMB (0.73%) and GNLY (2.86%).

   3. TGF-beta Signaling Pathway (TGFB1 - TGFBR1 / TGFBR2):
      - Mechanism: Secreted and cell-surface presentation of active TGF-beta, delivering potent immunosuppressive signals that inhibit CD4+ T cell activation, proliferation, and pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion.
      - Quantitative Evidence: KIR+CD8+ T cells express high levels of TGFB1 (54.43% positivity, mean expression 2.422; significantly higher than naive CD4+ T cells at 16.94%, mean 0.549). Pathogenic CD4+ T cells express both receptor subunits: TGFBR1 (2.10%) and TGFBR2 (22.45%), providing an active receptor complex for suppressive signaling.

   4. C-Type Lectin Pathway (CLEC2D / CLEC2B - KLRB1):
      - Mechanism: CLEC2D (LLT1) and CLEC2B bind to the inhibitory/modulatory C-type lectin-like receptor KLRB1 (CD161).
      - Quantitative Evidence: KLRB1 (CD161) is a hallmark surface marker of gut-homing pathogenic Th1/Th17 cells in celiac disease, expressed on 32.00% of pathogenic CD4+ T cells (mean expression 2.566; a 5.4-fold enrichment over naive CD4+ T cells at 5.89%, mean 0.439). KIR+CD8+ T cells strongly express the cognate ligands CLEC2B (56.49% positivity) and CLEC2D (44.46% positivity), yielding significant CellChat communication probabilities (prob = 0.0135 and 0.0048, p < 0.001).

   5. Synaptic Adhesion and Costimulatory Axis (CD99, SELPLG - SELL, MIF - CD74, CD2 - CD58):
      - Mechanism: Formation of a tight immunological synapse required for directional exocytosis of lytic granules and stable receptor engagement.
      - Quantitative Evidence:
        * CD99 - CD99: Homophilic interaction with high communication probability (prob = 0.1461, p < 0.001), expressed on 98.58% of KIR+CD8+ T cells and 83.36% of pathogenic CD4+ T cells.
        * SELPLG - SELL: PSGL-1 (expressed on 70.89% of KIR+CD8+ T cells) engages L-selectin (expressed on 62.24% of pathogenic CD4+ T cells) with prob = 0.0524 (p < 0.001).
        * MIF - (CD74+CD44/CXCR4): Inferred interaction with prob = 0.0782 (CD74+CD44) and 0.0691 (CD74+CXCR4), p < 0.001.
        * CD2 - CD58: High co-expression of CD2 and CD58 facilitates cell-to-cell adhesion during cytotoxic targeting.

3. Conclusion:
Beyond MHC class I-mediated recognition, the suppressive function and cytotoxic targeting by KIR+CD8+ T cells against pathogenic gliadin-specific CD4+ T cells operate via a coordinated multi-tier mechanism: (1) selective death receptor apoptosis via FASLG–FAS, (2) lethal cytolytic pore-formation via Perforin/Granzyme/Granulysin degranulation, (3) bystander cytokine-mediated suppression through TGFB1–TGFBR1/2, (4) immune checkpoint modulation through CLEC2D/B–KLRB1 (CD161), and (5) stable immunological synapse anchoring through CD99, SELPLG–SELL, and CD2–CD58.

QUESTION:
To identify potential cellular biomarkers for SLE diagnosis, which circulating immune cell populations show significantly altered frequencies in SLE patients compared to healthy controls?

FINAL ANSWER:
In this large-scale single-cell RNA sequencing PBMC cohort comprising 1,263,676 cells across 261 unique donors (162 systemic lupus erythematosus [SLE] patients and 99 healthy controls), multiple circulating immune cell populations exhibit statistically significant frequency alterations (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q < 0.05 from donor-level Mann-Whitney U tests and multivariable regression models adjusting for patient age and biological sex).

1. SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED CELL POPULATIONS IN SLE:
- Classical Monocytes (cM): Markedly expanded from 18.10% in healthy controls to 28.54% in SLE patients (mean difference: +10.44 percentage points; fold change: 1.58x; Mann-Whitney p = 1.45e-14, FDR q = 7.99e-14; Age/Sex-adjusted p = 9.59e-13). They represent the largest cellular expansion in peripheral blood, reflecting systemic innate immune activation driven by type I interferon signaling.
- Non-Classical Monocytes (ncM): Significantly elevated from 3.04% in controls to 4.35% in SLE (mean difference: +1.31 percentage points; fold change: 1.43x; p = 3.38e-5, FDR q = 7.44e-5; Age/Sex-adjusted p = 1.20e-2).
- Proliferating Lymphocytes: More than doubled from 0.38% in controls to 0.87% in SLE (mean difference: +0.49 percentage points; fold change: 2.28x; p = 1.16e-9, FDR q = 3.18e-9; Age/Sex-adjusted p = 1.36e-12), driven by clonal expansion and high turnover of activated cytotoxic effector cells.
- Cytotoxic T/NK Subpopulations: Granzyme H-positive cytotoxic cells (CytoT_GZMH+) show a >2-fold expansion (6.49% to 14.08%; p = 1.41e-7, FDR q = 3.28e-7), and Granzyme K-positive cytotoxic cells (CytoT_GZMK+) increase from 6.01% to 8.50% (p = 2.65e-5, FDR q = 4.64e-5).
- CD4+ Effector Memory (T4_em) and Regulatory T Cells (T4_reg): Relative increases within the remaining CD4+ compartment (T4_em: 8.66% to 13.00%, p = 1.35e-11; T4_reg: 3.00% to 4.69%, p = 3.33e-13).
- Atypical B Cells (B_atypical / age-associated B cells): Doubled in SLE (0.36% to 0.72%, fold change: 1.98x; p = 5.65e-4, FDR q = 8.79e-4), serving as pathogenic autoantibody precursors.
- Plasmablasts (PB): While rare in stable/managed patients, circulating plasmablasts expand 2.61-fold in active SLE flare patients compared to healthy controls (0.25% vs 0.10%, p = 1.79e-3; and 2.27-fold higher than managed SLE, p = 8.60e-4), representing a highly sensitive cellular biomarker of acute disease flare and active autoantibody production.

2. SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED CELL POPULATIONS IN SLE:
- CD4-Positive Alpha-Beta T Cells: Severely depleted from 37.46% in healthy controls to 24.77% in SLE patients (mean difference: -12.69 percentage points; fold change: 0.66x; Mann-Whitney p = 1.45e-18, FDR q = 1.60e-17; Age/Sex-adjusted p = 3.29e-18). High-resolution subtyping reveals this drop is heavily driven by naive CD4+ T cells (T4_naive), which collapse by nearly half from 34.30% to 18.47% (p = 6.26e-23, FDR q = 8.76e-22).
- Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cells (pDCs): Cut nearly in half from 0.57% in controls to 0.30% in SLE (mean difference: -0.27 percentage points; fold change: 0.52x; p = 2.03e-11, FDR q = 7.44e-11; Age/Sex-adjusted p = 5.02e-8). This reduction reflects activation-induced extravasation and homing into target inflamed tissues (e.g., skin, kidneys, lymph nodes).
- Mucosal-Associated Invariant T (MAIT) Cells (T_mait): Drastically reduced by ~65% in SLE (from 2.75% in controls to 0.98% in SLE; fold change: 0.35x; p = 1.33e-17, FDR q = 9.29e-17), reflecting chronic activation-induced cell death and peripheral tissue homing.
- Conventional Memory B Cells (B_mem): Significantly reduced from 6.60% to 4.01% (fold change: 0.61x; p = 1.42e-10, FDR q = 3.97e-10).
- Conventional Dendritic Cells (cDCs): Moderately decreased from 1.51% to 1.34% (fold change: 0.88x; p = 2.96e-3, FDR q = 5.43e-3).

3. POPULATIONS WITHOUT SIGNIFICANT BROAD-LEVEL FREQUENCY SHIFTS:
- Total pan-B cells (12.34% in controls vs 12.07% in SLE; p = 0.070, FDR q = 0.086), total CD8+ T cells (18.45% vs 20.64%; p = 0.193, FDR q = 0.213), and natural killer cells (7.97% vs 6.94%; p = 0.059, FDR q = 0.082) do not display significant net frequency changes at the broad lineage level, though each exhibits profound internal compositional remodelling into cytotoxic, memory, or exhausted effector states.

SUMMARY OF KEY CELLULAR BIOMARKERS FOR SLE DIAGNOSIS:
The most robust cellular diagnostic profile of SLE in peripheral blood consists of:
1. Expansion of classical monocytes (cM, >25% of PBMCs)
2. Pronounced lymphopenia marked by severe depletion of naive CD4+ T cells (T4_naive)
3. Significant peripheral depletion of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) and MAIT cells
4. Concurrent elevations of proliferating lymphocytes, cytotoxic effector subsets (CytoT_GZMH+), atypical B cells, and flare-associated surges in circulating plasmablasts.

An analysis of 1,242,772 peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) across 256 well-annotated donors (107 Asian: 83 SLE, 24 healthy control; 149 European American: 75 SLE, 74 healthy control) demonstrates that while certain lupus hallmarks are shared pan-ancestrally, distinct lymphoid and myeloid shifts differentiate the two populations:

   - Proliferating Lymphocyte Elevation: Circulating proliferating lymphocytes increase significantly in both cohorts (+0.34% in Europeans, +0.57% in Asians).

2. Ancestry-Divergent Immunopathology:
   - Exaggerated CD4+ T Cell Collapse in Asians: While both groups experience CD4+ lymphopenia, the reduction in Asian SLE patients is more than 2.6-fold larger than in European Americans (-20.23% points [from 42.17% down to 21.94%] vs. -7.68% points [from 35.96% down to 28.28%]; interaction beta = -12.17% points, p = 1.32e-5, FDR = 1.45e-4). This is driven specifically by a severe depletion of naive CD4+ T cells (-27.31% points of total T cells in Asians vs. -16.34% in Europeans; interaction p = 2.87e-3, FDR = 0.0201).
   - Robust Cytotoxic CD8+ Expansion and CD4/CD8 Inversion: Asian SLE patients exhibit a notable expansion of CD8+ T cells (+4.55% points vs. -0.51% in Europeans; p = 0.026), predominantly driven by cytotoxic GZMH+ CD8+ T cells (+13.53% points vs. +7.37% in Europeans; reaching 23.88% of total T cells in Asian SLE). Consequently, the CD4/CD8 ratio drops severely in Asians (mean 2.58 in controls to 1.21 in SLE; median 2.38 to 0.92; interaction beta = -0.6053, p = 1.23e-3). Over half of Asian SLE patients exhibit an inverted CD4/CD8 ratio (< 1.0) compared to only 21.3% of European SLE patients (55.4% [46/83] vs. 21.3% [16/75]; Odds Ratio = 4.58, 95% CI: 2.22-9.47, Fisher's exact p = 1.79e-5).
   - Differential Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell (pDC) Fluctuations: European Americans exhibit a prominent baseline circulating pDC compartment in controls (0.65%) that drops by over 50% in SLE to 0.32% (p = 2.92e-6), consistent with peripheral pDC homing into target inflamed tissues. Analysis of targeted-panel genomic profiling (MSK-IMPACT; 1,803 unambiguously classified primary and metastatic samples: 1,422 HR+/HER2-, 141 HR+/HER2+, 66 HR-/HER2+, and 174 TNBC) demonstrates that breast cancer receptor subtypes exhibit divergent mutational profiles, copy-number architectures, and pathway dependencies, while harboring clinically actionable molecular subcohorts that cross conventional immunohistochemical boundaries:

  * Mutational Architecture: Dominated by high rates of PI3K/AKT pathway mutations (PIK3CA: 41.1% [585/1,422], AKT1: 6.3% [89/1,422], PTEN alterations: 9.0% [128/1,422]), luminal transcription factors (GATA3: 17.5% [249/1,422]), cell-cell adhesion loss (CDH1: 18.7% [266/1,422], hallmark of invasive lobular carcinoma), and MAP-kinase pathway regulators (MAP3K1: 9.0%, MAP2K4: 4.0%).

  * Genome Stability: Exhibits the lowest rate of TP53 mutations (26.8%) and a low median TMB (0.100 nonsynonymous mut/Mb).

- HR+/HER2+ (Triple-Positive; n=141):
  * Hybrid Genomic Phenotype: Concurrently retains luminal mutational characteristics (PIK3CA mutations: 38.3%, GATA3 mutations: 17.0%, CCND1 amplifications: 19.9%, FGFR1 amplifications: 10.6%) alongside the canonical 17q12 ERBB2 amplicon.
  * ERBB2 & CDK12 Co-Amplification: High-level ERBB2 amplification occurs in 66.7% (94/141) of sequenced tumors, with 50.4% (71/141) harboring concurrent amplification of the adjacent transcription kinase CDK12.
  * Intermediate Genomic Instability: Shows an intermediate TP53 mutation frequency (45.4%), significantly higher than HR+/HER2- (26.8%, p=6.4e-6) but lower than HR-/HER2+ (78.8%, p=1.2e-5).

- HR-/HER2+ (HER2-Enriched; n=66):
  * Predominant Chromosomal Instability: Marked by high TP53 mutation rates (78.8%) and the highest frequency of high-level ERBB2 amplification (86.4%, 57/66) and CDK12 co-amplification (56.1%, 37/66).
  * Absence of Luminal Drivers: Complete absence of GATA3 mutations (0.0%, p=1.06e-10 vs HR+) and ESR1 mutations (0.0%).
  * Secondary RTK/MAPK Resistance Drivers: Shows a significantly higher rate of inactivating NF1 alterations (16.7% vs 4.6% in HR+/HER2-, p=1.6e-4), representing an alternative bypass driver of MAPK activation.

- TNBC (Triple-Negative / Basal-Like; n=174):
  * Extreme Checkpoint Loss and Replication Stress: Defined by near-ubiquitous TP53 inactivation (89.7%, 156/174) and frequent biallelic RB1 disruption via mutation (9.8%) and homozygous deep deletion (6.3%), totaling 16.1% (28/174) RB1 alterations (5.2-fold higher than HR+/HER2-, p=1.05e-14).

-----------------------------------------------------------

a) PI3K/AKT/PTEN Pathway-Altered Cohorts (Targetable with Alpelisib, Inavolisib, Capivasertib):

Key findings from targeted-panel (MSK-IMPACT) genomic profiling of endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- breast cancers:

1. Statistical Association and Mutual Exclusivity:
   - In post-hormonal therapy HR+/HER2- metastatic tumors (N = 687), ESR1 nonsynonymous mutations are detected in 104 samples (15.14%), while core MAPK pathway mutations (involving NF1, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF, RAF1, ARAF, MAP2K1, MAP2K2, MAPK1) are present in 63 samples (9.17%).
   - Only 2 tumors harbor both an ESR1 mutation and a core MAPK pathway mutation (expected under independence: 9.54), demonstrating significant mutual exclusivity (Fisher's exact test odds ratio = 0.1678, 95% CI: 0.021 - 0.627, p = 0.0028).
   - When including functional copy-number alterations (focal amplifications of KRAS, BRAF, RAF1, MAPK1, MAPK3, MAP2K1, MAP2K2 and deep deletions of NF1; total altered = 84, 12.23%), mutual exclusivity remains significant with only 5 co-occurring tumors (observed: 5 vs expected: 12.72; odds ratio = 0.3222, 95% CI: 0.108 - 0.812, p = 0.0092).
   - After adjusting for nonsynonymous tumor mutational burden (TMB) in multivariable logistic regression, the mutual exclusivity remains highly robust (adjusted odds ratio = 0.0973, 95% CI: 0.021 - 0.452, p = 0.0029 for mutations; adjusted odds ratio = 0.2253, 95% CI: 0.082 - 0.621, p = 0.0040 for mutations and copy-number alterations).
   - Patient-level de-duplication (N = 610 unique patients) confirms the same pattern (mutations: OR = 0.1884, p = 0.0097; alterations: OR = 0.3512, p = 0.0260).
   - Testing individual pathway components reveals that NF1 inactivating alterations (the most frequent MAPK alteration in this cohort: 42 mutations, 5 deep deletions) are strongly mutually exclusive with ESR1 mutations (OR = 0.1283, p = 0.0130 for mutations; OR = 0.1133, p = 0.0054 for alterations, with only 1 co-occurrence).

2. Biological and Clinical Significance:
   - Both ESR1 activating mutations (such as p.D538G, p.Y537S/C/N, p.E380Q) and MAPK pathway alterations (principally NF1 loss-of-function, RAS/RAF hotspot mutations, and pathway amplifications) represent distinct, independent parallel mechanisms of acquired endocrine resistance.
   - ESR1 mutations confer ligand-independent, constitutive ER transcriptional activity, driving resistance specifically to aromatase inhibitors while remaining ER-dependent.
   - In contrast, MAPK pathway hyperactivation downregulates ER dependence and bypasses ER signaling by driving transcription factor phosphorylation and cell cycle progression independently of estrogen receptor engagement.
   - Because either alteration independently provides escape from hormonal blockade, a tumor rarely benefits from acquiring both, leading to strong mutual exclusivity in clinical endocrine-resistant cohorts.

Dabrafenib exhibits a predominantly DIVERGENT transcriptional response across the four primary human cell types, accompanied by a small, highly conserved core stress response module.

Key quantitative and biological findings supporting this conclusion:

1. Global Transcriptional Divergence and Low-to-Moderate Correlation:
   - Pairwise Pearson correlation of log2 fold changes across all 11,010 shared expressed genes is moderate among mesenchymal/contractile lineages (aortic smooth muscle cells [AoSMCs], skeletal muscle myoblasts [SkMMs], and dermal fibroblasts: r = 0.463 to 0.574, Spearman rho = 0.391 to 0.513), but low between melanocytes and all other cell types (r = 0.306 to 0.321, Spearman rho = 0.233 to 0.251).
   - Across the 6,303 genes differentially expressed in at least one cell type, correlation between melanocytes and the other lineages remains low (r = 0.380 to 0.387).
   - Overlap between differentially expressed gene (DEG) sets (FDR < 0.05) reveals substantial divergence: pairwise Jaccard similarity indices are only 0.275 to 0.303 between AoSMCs, SkMMs, and fibroblasts, and drop to 0.115 to 0.127 between melanocytes and the other cell types.

2. Marked Differences in Perturbation Magnitude and Sensitivity:
   - Cell types display dramatic differences in overall transcriptional responsiveness to dabrafenib. At FDR < 0.05:
     * AoSMCs: 5,050 DEGs (most sensitive)
     * Dermal Fibroblasts: 3,173 DEGs
     * SkMMs: 3,026 DEGs
     * Melanocytes: 1,355 DEGs (least sensitive, ~3.7-fold fewer DEGs than AoSMCs)
   - Dose sensitivity also diverges sharply: at the lowest tested concentration (9.5 nM), primary melanocytes show almost no transcriptional alteration (only 1 DEG at FDR < 0.05), whereas AoSMCs (239 DEGs), fibroblasts (187 DEGs), and SkMMs (130 DEGs) already mount widespread transcriptional responses.

3. Directionally Opposed (Discordant) Gene Regulation:
   - 54 genes exhibit statistically significant opposite regulatory directions between melanocytes and other lineages (FDR < 0.05 in both).
   - Most notably, key structural and cytoskeletal genes ACTB (logFC: melanocytes = +0.28 vs. AoSMC = -0.83, fibroblasts = -0.42, SkMM = -0.43) and ACTG1 (logFC: melanocytes = +0.17 vs. AoSMC = -0.69, fibroblasts = -0.20, SkMM = -0.36) are significantly upregulated in melanocytes but repressed in smooth muscle, skeletal muscle, and fibroblasts.
   - Cholesterol efflux transporter ABCA1 is repressed in melanocytes (-0.43) but induced in AoSMCs (+0.88), SkMMs (+0.45), and fibroblasts (+0.35); polyamine regulator SAT1 is downregulated in melanocytes (-0.46) but upregulated in AoSMCs (+0.41), fibroblasts (+0.66), and SkMMs (+0.49).

4. Conserved Core Response Module:
   - Embedded within this divergent landscape is an invariant core of 265 genes altered across all four lineages (FDR < 0.05), of which 232 genes (87.5%) share identical directionality:
     * Conserved Upregulation (101 genes): Induction of the ATF4-dependent Integrated Stress Response (ISR) and amino acid biosynthetic/transport machinery (e.g., ATF4, DDIT3/CHOP, TRIB3, CHAC1, SLC7A11, SLC1A5, PHGDH, PSAT1, SHMT2, MTHFD2, and multiple aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases GARS1, YARS1, SARS1, WARS1).
     * Conserved Downregulation (131 genes): Coordinated suppression of actomyosin, cytoskeletal organization, and focal adhesion elements (e.g., MYL9, TPM1, TPM2, RHOA, CAV1, CAVIN1, DSTN) and the oxytocin receptor (OXTR).
   - In addition, MAPK feedback inhibitors DUSP6 and SPRY2 are upregulated across all four lineages, consistent with paradoxical activation of wild-type RAF dimers by dabrafenib in non-mutant backgrounds; however, downstream immediate-early transcriptional outputs (FOS, EGR1) diverge significantly across tissues (robustly induced in fibroblasts and myoblasts, but quiescent in melanocytes and AoSMCs).

Conclusion:
Dabrafenib induces a predominantly divergent transcriptional response across primary human cell types, characterized by low cross-cell-type correlation, distinct dose sensitivity, tissue-specific functional programs (e.g., severe contractile and vascular remodeling in AoSMCs vs. relative transcriptional buffering in melanocytes), and opposing regulation of cytoskeletal and metabolic genes, while sharing a narrow, conserved ATF4-mediated integrated stress response module.

SYSTEMATIC DISCOVERY AND TRANSLATIONAL PRIORITIZATION OF SYNTHETIC-LETHAL PARTNERS FOR LOSS-OF-FUNCTION EVENTS IN BREAST CANCER (BRCA)
========================================================================================================================

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
-----------------
Using integrated multi-omics datasets spanning cancer cell line CRISPR knockouts (CCLE DepMap, 18,119 genes across 195 cell lines), damaging loss-of-function mutation matrices (74 unique breast cancer models across 19,616 genes), and machine-learning predicted patient-level dependency scores (1,966 genes across 1,099 TCGA primary BRCA tumors), we identified, validated, and clinically prioritized synthetic-lethal (SL) partner vulnerabilities for recurrent tumor-suppressor loss-of-function events in breast cancer.

Our analytical framework integrated four complementary layers of evidence:
1. Multivariate regularized Lasso regression on cell-line DepMap dependency scores to isolate conditionally independent genetic dependencies while controlling for co-occurring genomic alterations.
2. Pairwise Fisher's exact mutual-exclusivity testing across cell-line mutation profiles to identify evolutionary negative selection.
3. Mechanistic biological priors incorporating sequence/functional paralog redundancy and high-confidence physical protein-protein interactions (PPI).
4. Patient-level translational scoring across 1,099 TCGA BRCA primary tumors and current clinical/pharmacological tractability benchmarks (FDA-approved therapeutics, clinical trials, and selective chemical probes).


RECURRENT LOSS-OF-FUNCTION DRIVERS IN BRCA
------------------------------------------
Profiling 74 unique breast cancer cell line models identified recurrent damaging loss-of-function mutations across canonical tumor-suppressor pathways:
- TP53: 55/74 models (74.3% in cell lines; 27/36 matched DepMap models)
- PTEN: 11/74 models (14.9% in cell lines; 6/36 matched DepMap models)
- ARID1A: 8/74 models (10.8% in cell lines; 3/36 matched DepMap models)
- CDH1: 8/74 models (10.8% in cell lines; 2/36 matched DepMap models)
- NF1: 8/74 models (10.8% in cell lines; 5/36 matched DepMap models)
- BRCA2: 7/74 models (9.5% in cell lines; 2/36 matched DepMap models)
- BRCA1: 5/74 models (6.8% in cell lines; 4/36 matched DepMap models)


TOP PRIORITIZED SYNTHETIC-LETHAL PARTNERS BY TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE
---------------------------------------------------------------------

1. BRCA1 / BRCA2 Deficiency -> PARP1 (Rank 1)
   - Mechanism: DNA repair epistasis. PARP1 trapping prevents single-strand break repair, triggering replication fork collapse into double-strand breaks that require BRCA1/2-mediated homologous recombination (HR) for resolution.
   - Evidence: Lasso beta = -0.488 (p = 0.0299, Delta Dep = -0.201).
   - Biological Prior: Paralog / base excision repair pathway epistasis.
   - Translational Status: FDA-approved standard of care in BRCA-mutant breast cancer (Olaparib, Talazoparib).

2. BRCA1 / BRCA2 Deficiency -> POLQ (Rank 2)
   - Mechanism: Alternative non-homologous end joining (TMEJ) addiction. When homologous recombination is disabled, cells become strictly dependent on DNA Polymerase Theta (POLQ) for double-strand break repair.
   - Evidence: Lasso beta = -0.460 (p = 0.0719, Delta Dep = -0.227).
   - Biological Prior: Synthetic addiction to backup DSB repair pathway.
   - Translational Status: Active Phase I/II clinical trials (ART4215, novobiocin) for HR-deficient and PARP-inhibitor-resistant breast cancers.

3. ARID1A Loss -> ARID1B (Rank 3)
   - Mechanism: Paralog synthetic lethality in the SWI/SNF (BAF) chromatin remodeling complex. Loss of ARID1A forces residual BAF complexes to rely obligatorily on its mutually exclusive paralog ARID1B for complex assembly and chromatin targeting.
   - Evidence: Lasso beta = -1.240 (p = 0.00076, Delta Dep = -0.327).
   - Biological Prior: Canonical BAF subunit paralog exchange.
   - Translational Status: High-priority preclinical development; target for selective ARID1B PROTAC degraders and dual BAF ATPase inhibitors.

4. PTEN Loss -> PIK3CB (Rank 4)
   - Mechanism: Catalytic isoform addiction. PTEN loss leads to preferential survival dependency on the p110beta catalytic subunit (PIK3CB) rather than the canonical p110alpha isoform (PIK3CA).
   - Evidence: Lasso beta = -1.485 (p = 0.000005, Delta Dep = -0.435).
   - Biological Prior: Paralog catalytic isoform addiction.
   - Translational Status: Phase I/II clinical trials of selective p110beta inhibitors (AZD8186, GSK2636771) in PTEN-deficient solid tumors.

5. ARID1A Loss -> SMARCA2 (Rank 5)
   - Mechanism: Catalytic subunit addiction in SWI/SNF complexes. ARID1A-deficient cells display heightened vulnerability to depletion of the SWI/SNF ATPase subunit SMARCA2.
   - Evidence: Lasso beta = -0.667 (p = 0.0285, Delta Dep = -0.152).
   - Biological Prior: BAF catalytic ATPase paralog.
   - Translational Status: Active Phase I clinical trials of selective SMARCA2 degraders (PRT3789) for ARID1A- and SMARCA4-mutant cancers.

6. BRCA1 / BRCA2 Deficiency -> RAD51 (Rank 6)
   - Mechanism: Core homologous recombination machinery. Physical PPI complex interactor. Residual homologous recombination and replication fork protection require RAD51 nucleoprotein filament assembly.
   - Evidence: TCGA patient dependency mean = -1.089 (100.0% of 1,099 primary TCGA BRCA tumors exhibit strong dependency < -0.5).
   - Biological Prior: Direct physical PPI / core HR complex member.
   - Translational Status: Preclinical target validation (RAD51 small-molecule inhibitors, RI-1, IBR2).

7. TP53 Inactivation -> USP7 (Rank 7)
   - Mechanism: Deubiquitinase physical PPI network. USP7 regulates the stability of the MDM2/MDM4/p53 feedback circuit and sustains DNA replication fork integrity.
   - Evidence: TCGA patient dependency mean = -0.743 (100.0% of 1,099 TCGA BRCA tumors exhibit strong dependency < -0.5).
   - Biological Prior: High-confidence direct physical PPI.
   - Translational Status: Preclinical chemical probes and USP7 inhibitors (FT671).

8. ARID1A Loss -> PIK3CA (Rank 8)
   - Mechanism: Oncogenic pathway crosstalk. ARID1A loss frequently co-operates with hyperactivated PI3K/AKT signaling to drive breast tumorigenesis.
   - Evidence: Lasso beta = -0.400 (p = 0.0877, Delta Dep = -0.380). TCGA patient dependency mean = -0.530 (64.9% of 1,099 TCGA BRCA tumors exhibit strong dependency < -0.5).
   - Biological Prior: Epigenetic-to-kinase signaling crosstalk.
   - Translational Status: FDA-approved PI3Kalpha inhibitor (Alpelisib) in breast cancer.

9. CDH1 Loss -> ERBB2 (Rank 9)
   - Mechanism: Receptor tyrosine kinase signaling crosstalk. Inactivation of E-cadherin (CDH1), characteristic of invasive lobular breast carcinoma, confers elevated dependence on HER2/HER3 receptor signaling networks.
   - Evidence: CCLE Delta Dep = -0.483; TCGA patient dependency mean = -0.400 (12.2% of TCGA BRCA patients strongly dependent < -0.5).
   - Biological Prior: Cell adhesion to growth factor receptor crosstalk.
   - Translational Status: FDA-approved HER2-targeted agents (Trastuzumab, Trastuzumab deruxtecan, Neratinib).

10. NF1 Inactivation -> RAF1 / MAP2K1 / MAP2K2 (Rank 10)
    - Mechanism: Direct RAS pathway effector dependencies. NF1 inactivation releases neurofibromin-mediated RAS inhibition, causing constitutive downstream pathway addiction to C-Raf (RAF1) and MEK1/2.
    - Evidence: Lasso beta = -0.465 (p = 0.0272, Delta Dep = -0.235).
    - Biological Prior: Direct physical PPI and core kinase pathway cascade.
    - Translational Status: FDA-approved MEK inhibitors (Trametinib, Selumetinib) and clinical-stage pan-RAF inhibitors.


MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY FINDINGS IN MUTATION MATRIX

CONCLUSION AND CLINICAL TRANSLATION
------------------------------------
Integrating regularized Lasso regression, mutual-exclusivity statistics, paralog/PPI constraints, and patient-level TCGA dependency scoring prioritizes:
1. Approved synthetic-lethal clinical standards: PARP1 inhibition (Olaparib, Talazoparib) for BRCA1/2-mutated breast cancer, and PIK3CA inhibition (Alpelisib) for ARID1A-associated PI3K pathway dependency.

PRIORITIZING DRUGGABLE PROTEIN TARGETS FOR PANCREATIC CANCER (PDAC)
========================================================================

Based on the CPTAC pan-cancer proteogenomic druggability dataset (Cell 2024), candidate drug targets for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) were prioritized by integrating two rigorous criteria:
1. Statistically significant protein overexpression in primary PDAC tumors compared to normal adjacent pancreatic tissue (adj. p <= 0.01).
2. Statistically significant gene knockout dependency in matched PDAC cancer cell line lineages based on DepMap CRISPR-Cas9 screens (adj. p <= 0.01).

Across the proteome (5,262 proteins evaluated in Table S3A), exactly 1,431 proteins satisfy both significant tumor overexpression and CRISPR knockout dependency in PDAC. When mapped to established druggability tiers (Table S2A/S2B/S2C/S2D), 222 proteins are characterized as druggable targets across Tiers 1 to 5.

Below is the structured breakdown and prioritization of these promising targets:

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. OVERVIEW OF DRUGGABLE TARGETS BY TIER (Total = 222 targets)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Tier 1 (Targets of FDA-approved antineoplastic drugs): 34 targets
- Tier 2 (Targets of FDA-approved non-oncology drugs / repurposing): 32 targets
- Tier 3 (Targets with investigational drugs in clinical trials or chemical probes): 61 targets
- Tier 4 (Potentially druggable genes via DGIdb druggable genome): 73 targets
- Tier 5 (Cell-surface membrane proteins accessible for biologics / ADCs / CAR-T): 22 targets

Therapeutic Window Stratification:
- Non-essential / Lineage-selective (DepMap Common Essential = 0): 190 targets (85.6%)
  (Favorable therapeutic window; lower anticipated on-target systemic toxicity)
- Pan-cancer essential (DepMap Common Essential = 1): 32 targets (14.4%)
  (Potent tumor-inhibitory activity, but narrower window due to core housekeeping roles)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. HIGHEST-PRIORITY ACTIONABLE TARGETS (TIER 1: APPROVED CANCER DRUGS)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total: 34 targets. These have immediate clinical relevance with approved oncology agents:

A. Oncogenic Driver and MAPK Signaling:
   - KRAS (Essential): The central oncogenic driver in >90% of PDAC; targeted by covalent KRAS inhibitors (e.g., sotorasib for G12C, as well as emerging G12D/pan-KRAS inhibitors).
   - MAP2K2 / MEK2 (Non-essential): Key downstream kinase in the KRAS-MAPK pathway; targeted by approved MEK inhibitors (cobimetinib, trametinib, binimetinib).

B. Receptor Tyrosine Kinases and Growth Signaling:
   - MET / c-Met (Non-essential; active across 5 CPTAC cancer cohorts): Targeted by capmatinib, tepotinib, crizotinib, cabozantinib, and amivantamab.
   - ERBB2 / HER2 (Non-essential; active across 4 cohorts): Targeted by trastuzumab, pertuzumab, lapatinib, tucatinib, and trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1).
   - PDGFRB (Non-essential): Targeted by sunitinib, pazopanib, regorafenib, and sorafenib.
   - CSF1R (Non-essential): Macrophage colony-stimulating factor receptor, mediating tumor-associated immunosuppressive macrophage infiltration; targeted by pexidartinib and sunitinib.
   - Other kinases: DDR2, YES1, SRC, BTK, IKBKB (all non-essential).

   - NECTIN4 (Non-essential; active across 4 cohorts): Targeted by enfortumab vedotin.
   - F3 / Tissue Factor (Non-essential): Targeted by tisotumab vedotin.

D. DNA Replication, Metabolism, and Core Machinery:
   - RRM1 and RRM2 (Essential): Ribonucleotide reductase catalytic subunits, the primary molecular targets of gemcitabine (standard first-line PDAC chemotherapy).
   - TOP2A (Essential): Topoisomerase II alpha, targeted by etoposide, doxorubicin, and mitoxantrone.
   - DNMT1 (Essential): DNA methyltransferase 1, targeted by azacitidine and decitabine.
   - XPO1 / Exportin-1 (Essential): Targeted by selinexor.
   - MTOR (Essential): Targeted by everolimus and temsirolimus.
   - GART and ATIC (Non-essential): Purine synthesis enzymes targeted by pemetrexed and methotrexate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total: 32 targets (28 non-essential, 4 essential):

- ANO1 / TMEM16A (Non-essential): Calcium-activated chloride channel driving tumor cell proliferation; inhibited by crofelemer.
- MMP7 (Matrix metalloproteinase 7; Non-essential): Promotes tumor invasion and desmoplasia; inhibited by doxycycline.
- FNTA (Farnesyltransferase alpha; Essential): Mediates post-translational prenylation/membrane anchoring of Ras; targeted by lonafarnib.
- TFRC (Transferrin receptor 1; Essential; active across 7 cohorts): Mediates iron uptake essential for tumor proliferation.

- CLDN18 / Claudin 18.2 (Non-essential): Tight junction protein overexpressed on pancreatic adenocarcinoma cells; targeted by zolbetuximab (IMAB362).
- FAP / Fibroblast activation protein alpha (Non-essential): Hallmark marker of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) driving PDAC desmoplasia; targeted by FAP-directed radioligands and CAR-T therapies.
- SLC3A2 / CD98hc (Non-essential; active across 7 cohorts): Amino acid transporter subunit involved in cystine import and prevention of ferroptosis.
- CA9 / Carbonic anhydrase IX (Non-essential; active across 5 cohorts): Key regulator of intracellular pH in hypoxic PDAC microenvironments.
- CD276 / B7-H3 (Non-essential; active across 5 cohorts): Immune checkpoint ligand overexpressed on PDAC cells and tumor vasculature.
- Kinases and Epigenetic Regulators: AKT1, AKT2, TBK1, MAPK14 (p38), MAPKAPK2 (MK2), LIMK1, RIPK3, KDM3A, KDM5B, CARM1, PTPN1.
- Essential Tier 3 Kinases: CDK1, CDK7, AURKB, CSNK1A1, PIK3C3, PIP5K1A, BCL2L1.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. CELL-SURFACE ACCESSIBLE TARGETS FOR BIOLOGICS & ADCS (TIER 5)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total: 22 targets (100% non-essential):
Because all 22 targets are non-essential for general cellular viability but overexpressed at the protein level on the plasma membrane in PDAC, they represent ideal targets for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), monoclonal antibodies, and T-cell engagers:
- SLC2A1 / GLUT1 (Active across 5 cohorts): Glucose transporter 1, facilitating metabolic hyper-glycolysis.
- ADGRG1 / GPR56 (Active across 5 cohorts): Adhesion GPCR involved in cell adhesion and signaling.
- CDH3 (P-cadherin) and CDH2 (N-cadherin): Classical cadherins mediating epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and metastasis.
- CSPG4 (NG2): Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4.
- PVR / CD155: Immune checkpoint ligand for TIGIT and CD226.
- PODXL (Podocalyxin-like): Marker of cancer stem cells and aggressive invasiveness.
- Additional Tier 5 targets: ATRAID, ATRN, CD53, CD9, FAS, HLA-C, ITGA1, ITM2B, LDLR, LRP1, PILRA, SGCD, SGCE, SLC8B1.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONCLUSION
------------------------------------------------------------------------
In summary, 1,431 proteins exhibit statistically significant tumor overexpression and CRISPR knockout dependency in PDAC, of which 222 belong to established druggability tiers (34 in Tier 1, 32 in Tier 2, 61 in Tier 3, 73 in Tier 4, and 22 in Tier 5). Prioritizing across actionable pathways highlights:
1. KRAS-MAPK signaling: KRAS, MAP2K2, PAK1, and downstream AKT/MTOR.
2. Receptor tyrosine kinases: MET, ERBB2, PDGFRB, and CSF1R.
3. Tumor microenvironment and stroma: FAP, CSF1R, and CD276.
4. Clinically actionable cell-surface targets for ADCs: NECTIN4, CLDN18 (Claudin 18.2), F3 (Tissue Factor), SLC2A1, and CDH3.
5. Metabolic and survival vulnerabilities: RRM1, RRM2, LDHA, SLC3A2, and CA9.

TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF EXERCISE TRAINING RESPONSE IN SKELETAL MUSCLE (SKM-VL) - DA-6-2

1. OVERVIEW AND SUMMARY OF DYNAMICS
Gene expression in vastus lateralis skeletal muscle (SKM-VL) exhibits a pronounced, multi-phase temporal remodeling over the 8-week progressive endurance training course. Across the 766 training-regulated transcriptomic features (IHW FDR q < 0.05), the transcriptional program undergoes a distinct temporal phase transition:
- Early training (Weeks 1 and 2): Marked by low cross-sex correlation (r = 0.134 at 1w; r = 0.070 at 2w) and pronounced sexual dimorphism, characterized by rapid transcriptional activation in females and substantial divergence in extracellular matrix and structural programs.
- Chronic training (Weeks 4 and 8): Marked by a strong progressive convergence toward a shared physiological adaptation program (r = 0.430 at 4w; r = 0.633 at 8w; z-score r = 0.720 at 8w), with 99.6% directional concordance among co-regulated features by 8 weeks.

2. QUANTITATIVE TIMEWISE TRAJECTORIES IN MALES AND FEMALES
The magnitude and velocity of gene expression changes differ substantially between sexes across the training timeline:
- Females display a rapid, monotonic expansion of regulated genes:
  * 1 week: 220 genes significant (p < 0.05; 136 Up, 84 Down)
  * 2 weeks: 329 genes significant (p < 0.05; 162 Up, 167 Down)
  * 4 weeks: 501 genes significant (p < 0.05; 312 Up, 189 Down)
  * 8 weeks: 532 genes significant (p < 0.05; 342 Up, 190 Down)
- Males exhibit a delayed, bifurcated response with an abrupt surge at chronic stages:
  * 1 week: 145 genes significant (p < 0.05; 85 Up, 60 Down)
  * 2 weeks: 134 genes significant (p < 0.05; 63 Up, 71 Down)
  * 4 weeks: 176 genes significant (p < 0.05; 114 Up, 62 Down)
  * 8 weeks: 379 genes significant (p < 0.05; 217 Up, 162 Down; >2-fold increase from week 4)

Co-significant features across sexes increase from only 33 genes at 1w (24 concordant, 9 discordant) and 39 genes at 2w (23 concordant, 16 discordant) to 107 genes at 4w (105 concordant, 2 discordant) and 265 genes at 8w (264 concordant, exactly 1 discordant).

3. PREDOMINANT SHARED AND SEX-SPECIFIC TEMPORAL PATTERNS
Unsupervised trajectory clustering and functional pathway dissection reveal four predominant expression patterns:

(A) Shared Progressive Mitochondrial and Metabolic Upregulation (Cluster 1; N = 279 genes, 36.4%):
- Pattern: Progressive, sustained upregulation in both sexes, emerging earlier and stronger in females (mean logFC: +0.307 at 1w, +0.375 at 2w, +0.558 at 4w, +0.454 at 8w) and steadily accumulating in males (mean logFC: +0.160 at 1w, +0.167 at 2w, +0.326 at 4w, +0.309 at 8w).
- Biological Program: Massive induction of oxidative phosphorylation machinery across all 13 mitochondrial genome-encoded subunits (Mt-nd1-6, Mt-co1-3, Mt-cyb, Mt-atp6/8), dozens of nuclear-encoded respiratory chain components (Ndufa/b/s Complex I subunits, Cox4i1/Cox5a/Cox6/Cox7 Complex IV subunits, Uqcrc1/2 Complex III subunits, and Atp5f1/mc/pd/pf/po ATP synthase subunits).
- Key Drivers: Mitochondrial creatine kinases show the largest activation in skeletal muscle: Ckmt1 (logFC reaches +4.94 in males, +3.29 in females) and Ckmt2 (logFC +0.82 in females, +0.49 in males at 8w, p = 2.3e-15). Concomitant upregulation of fatty acid oxidation and lipid mobilization enzymes (Lpl, Fabp4, Lipe, Acsl1, Acox2, Acads, Acadvl), pyruvate carriers (Mpc1, Mpc2), and angiogenic vascular factors (Vegfb, Cdh5, Emcn, Apln).
- Interpretation: The primary, universal aerobic adaptation of skeletal muscle to sustained endurance exercise, expanding electron transport capacity, mitochondrial energy shuttling, and capillary perfusion.

(B) Shared Chronic Transcriptional and Stress Repression (Cluster 0; N = 253 genes, 33.0%):
- Pattern: Sustained downregulation across the training timeline, initiating early in females (1w-2w) and culminating at 8w in both sexes (mean logFC at 8w: -0.296 in females, -0.297 in males).
- Biological Program: Coordinated shutoff of immediate-early stress response and AP-1 transcription factors (Fos: logFC = -1.61 in females, -1.02 in males; Egr1: logFC = -1.12 in females, -0.67 in males; Btg2), fast-twitch/glycolytic contractile components (parvalbumin Pvalb: logFC = -0.46 in females, -0.46 in males; SERCA1 fast Ca2+ pump Atp2a1: -0.19 in males), glycolytic and glycogenolytic enzymes (Phka1, Phkb, Pgk1, Ldha, Gpi), and ubiquitin-proteasome E3 ligase machinery (Fem1c, Ube2d1, Asb16).
- Interpretation: Muscular habituation to recurrent exercise bouts, reducing cellular stress-signaling cascades and repressing glycolytic, fast-fiber programs in favor of fatigue-resistant slow-oxidative efficiency (supported by strong induction of myoglobin Mb: logFC = +0.70 in females, +0.67 in males).

(C) Sex-Dimorphic Acute Matrix Remodeling and Proliferation (Cluster 3; N = 95 genes, 12.4%):
- Pattern: Extreme sexual divergence during early training (Weeks 1 and 2), followed by return toward sedentary baseline by Week 8.
- Biological Program: Extracellular matrix (ECM) collagens (Col1a1, Col5a1, Col5a2, Col6a1, Col8a2, Col11a1), matricellular organizers and elastic fiber components (Tnmd, Ltbp2, Emilin3, Cilp, Fbn1, Lox), and cell cycle proliferation drivers (Mki67, Top2a, Prc1, Kif22).
- Sex Difference: In females, these genes are acutely upregulated at 1w and 2w (e.g., Col11a1 logFC = +2.02 at 1w; Col8a2 logFC = +0.87 at 2w; Tnmd logFC = +1.73 at 1w; Mki67 logFC = +2.11 at 2w). In contrast, in males, these exact matrix genes are strongly repressed during the same early period (Col11a1 logFC = -1.73 at 1w; Col8a2 logFC = -1.86 at 2w; Tnmd logFC = -2.13 at 1w; Ltbp2 logFC = -2.56 at 2w).
- Interpretation: Females mount an immediate structural and cellular rebuilding response involving fibroblast proliferation, satellite cell expansion, and collagen fibrillogenesis upon commencing treadmill running. Males suppress de novo collagen deposition during early training, delaying structural reorganization until later stages.

(D) Delayed Male-Biased Structural Reinforcement (Cluster 2; N = 139 genes, 18.1%):
- Pattern: Moderate early activation in males that evolves into sustained 8-week upregulation in both sexes (mean logFC at 8w: +0.368 in males, +0.188 in females).
- Biological Program: Sarcomeric and costameric structural scaffolding (Neb, Dmd, Ldb3, Klhl40, Xirp2, Tns1, Sorbs3), calcium signaling (Kcnma1, Cacna1a), and insulin-responsive glucose transport (Slc2a4 / GLUT4).
- Interpretation: Reinforcement of the mechanical stress-bearing apparatus and contractile transmission lines needed to sustain long-term mechanical power and glycogen repletion.

4. PERSISTENT SEX DISCORDANCE
At the chronic 8-week timepoint, exactly one gene displays statistically significant opposing regulation between sexes: Iqgap2 (IQ motif GTPase activating protein 2; ENSRNOG00000025406). Iqgap2 is persistently upregulated in males across all timepoints (logFC = +0.778 at 8w, p = 4.3e-4) but consistently repressed in females (logFC = -0.760 at 8w, p = 1.1e-4), reflecting sex-divergent actin-cytoskeleton signaling and GTPase regulation.

5. CONCLUSION
In summary, vastus lateralis skeletal muscle responds to endurance exercise through an initial phase of profound sexual divergence (dominated by acute ECM synthesis and proliferation in females versus early ECM repression in males) followed by an 8-week convergence onto a shared transcriptional program of mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid oxidation, fast-to-slow fiber transition, and stress-response habituation.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & MAIN FINDINGS
================================================================================

1. EXTENT OF MULTI-ORGAN COORDINATION:
Endurance exercise training elicits a response that is predominantly tissue-specific rather than universally coordinated. 
Across 9,800 training-regulated genes identified by transcriptome profiling across 19 tissues:
- 50.70% (4,969 genes) are regulated in only a single tissue.
- 49.30% (4,831 genes) are shared across two or more tissues.
- Only 4.92% (482 genes) are shared broadly across 5 or more tissues.
- Only 12 genes are shared across 8 or more tissues (the maximum observed sharing was in 9 tissues for ENSRNOG00000013961 and ENSRNOG00000031979).
- Across all 35,441 multi-omic features (including transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics), 69.28% are altered in only one tissue, and only 3.01% are shared across 5 or more tissues.
- The average pairwise trajectory correlation across all shared gene sets between distinct organs is weak (mean Pearson r = 0.101), demonstrating that while training exerts systemic physiological demands, organs execute distinct, cell-type-specific functional programs.

2. TISSUES EXHIBITING THE MOST SIMILAR CHANGES:
Across all pairwise comparisons evaluated across all molecular platforms and timepoints:
- Skeletal Muscle Subtypes (SKM-GN [Gastrocnemius] and SKM-VL [Vastus Lateralis]):
  Exhibit the highest coordination and similarity across the entire organism:
  * Highest Jaccard overlap: J = 0.1957 (218 shared DEGs).
  * Trajectory Pearson correlation: r = 0.8519 (p = 1.22 x 10^-246) across 1w, 2w, 4w, and 8w timepoints.
  * Chronic landmark correlation (8w): r = 0.9102 (p = 1.22 x 10^-84).
  * Directional concordance: 95.87% of shared genes change in the exact same direction at 8 weeks.
  * Shared biological response: Synchronous upregulation of oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial electron transport, and fatty acid oxidation genes (e.g., ENSRNOG00000050015, ENSRNOG00000062049, ENSRNOG00000011323) alongside repression of fast-glycolytic and protein catabolism markers.

- Circulatory and Immune Axis (Whole Blood [BLOOD] and Spleen [SPLEEN]):
  Form the second most coordinated tissue pair:
  * Jaccard overlap: J = 0.1443 (338 shared DEGs).
  * Trajectory Pearson correlation: r = 0.5487 (p = 3.82 x 10^-107).
  * Chronic landmark correlation (8w): r = 0.7763 (p = 2.50 x 10^-69).

3. TEMPORAL DYNAMICS AND RESPONSE KINETICS:
A clear temporal dichotomy divides the organism into two primary functional classes:
- Chronic Accumulators (peaking late at 4w or 8w):
  Whole Blood (86.4% late, 84.1% at 8w), Vastus Lateralis (85.5% late), Brown Adipose (79.0% late, 77.0% at 8w), Heart (72.0% late, 57.8% at 8w), Spleen (69.9% late, 60.4% at 8w), Liver (67.8% late, 51.1% at 8w), and Gastrocnemius (64.7% late, 53.4% at 8w). Based on the systematic analysis of the randomized phase-2 PRINCE trial (PICI0002) biomarker dataset at the on-treatment Cycle 2 Day 1 (C2D1) timepoint, circulating immune-cell frequencies do NOT significantly correlate with serum protein levels.

Key findings:
1. Data and Cohort Dimensions at C2D1:
   - Exactly 73 unique metastatic pancreatic cancer patients had matched on-treatment profiling at C2D1 across CyTOF immune cell frequencies and Olink serum proteomics.
   - Four circulating immune cell populations are measured at C2D1: Conventional DCs (N = 73), CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells (N = 65), HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4+ T Cells (N = 65), and HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8+ T Cells (N = 65).
   - Four serum proteins are measured at C2D1: CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-γ, and Soluble PD-1 (N = 73 each).

2. Correlative Evaluation:
   - Across all 16 pairwise combinations of immune cell frequencies and serum protein levels, all bivariate correlation coefficients are weak to negligible (|Spearman rho| <= 0.233; |Pearson r| <= 0.216).
   - The strongest nominal associations observed were weak inverse trends between CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells and CXCL9 (Spearman rho = -0.233, unadjusted p = 0.0615; Pearson r = -0.206, p = 0.0996) and CXCL10 (Spearman rho = -0.222, unadjusted p = 0.0756; Pearson r = -0.181, p = 0.1480).
   - After Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction for multiple testing across all 16 pairs, NO pairwise correlation achieves statistical significance (all Spearman FDR q-values >= 0.535; all Pearson FDR q-values >= 0.581; all Bonferroni-adjusted p-values >= 0.984).
   - Non-parametric Kendall tau rank correlation corroborates this lack of association (all tau values between -0.155 and +0.117; all FDR q-values >= 0.536).

3. Stratified and Multivariable Adjustments:
   - Soluble PD-1 levels vary strongly by treatment arm (Kruskal-Wallis p < 10^-9), reflecting nivolumab administration in Arms A1 and C2 compared to Arm B2.
   - Multivariable linear regression controlling for randomized treatment arm (Actual Arm: A1 vs B2 vs C2) confirmed that treatment confounding does not mask underlying relationships (all covariate-adjusted FDR q-values >= 0.588).
   - Within-arm subgroup analyses likewise identified no associations that survived multiple hypothesis testing correction (all arm-level FDR q-values >= 0.148).

Conclusion:
In this patient cohort at C2D1, on-treatment circulating immune-cell frequencies and serum protein levels represent decoupled biomarker compartments and do not exhibit significant correlation.
